Lygumai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiauliai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Lygumai's Jewish community, settled in the 18th century, reached 61 percent of the population by 1897 and was notably active in Zionism, running a training kibbutz affiliated with the HeKhalutz movement from 1934. Among its notable rabbis was Yisrael-Hillel, murdered during the 1929 Hebron massacre in Mandatory Palestine, and Dov Revel (1885–1940), first president of the Union of Rabbis of the United States. On June 28, 1941, the day German forces entered, around 1,000 Jews were present in the town, including refugees from surrounding areas; Lithuanian police locked them in a stable, and in the following weeks the men were shot in groups in a nearby forest while the remaining Jews were killed at Atkočiūnai Forest on July 23, 1941.
